facts: What starts many ocean food webs?
Phytoplankton use sunlight to produce food and support many marine food webs.
What organ lets most fish take oxygen from water?
Gills exchange gases between water and blood.
Coral polyps are animals that often live in colonies.
Why are microscopic algae important to many corals?
They provide much of the coral’s energy
They turn coral into rock instantly
Symbiotic algae photosynthesise and share energy with their coral hosts.
Corals lose or expel their symbiotic algae
Heat stress can cause corals to lose their algae and colour.
Salinity describes dissolved salt concentration in water.
What do ocean currents move around the planet?
Currents redistribute water, heat, nutrients, and organisms.
Density differences from temperature and salinity help drive circulation.
Where does most ocean photosynthesis occur?
Enough sunlight reaches the photic zone for photosynthesis.
What is special about the ocean twilight zone?
There is dim light but too little for much photosynthesis
The mesopelagic has low light and little to no photosynthesis.
Abyssal zones are deep, dark, high-pressure marine environments.
What happens to water pressure as ocean depth increases?
Pressure increases with the weight of water above.
Dolphins are mammals and breathe air.
What kind of animal is a whale?
Whales are marine mammals with lungs and nurse their young.
What kind of skeleton do sharks have?
Shark skeletons are made mainly of cartilage rather than bone.
How many arms does an octopus have?
Octopuses have eight arms lined with suckers.
Food webs show interconnected predator-prey and feeding relationships.
Why can biodiversity help ecosystem resilience?
Different species can support different ecological roles
Diverse communities can provide functional redundancy and resilience.
What gas drives modern ocean acidification when absorbed?
Dissolved carbon dioxide changes seawater chemistry and lowers pH.
Warming and other processes can reduce dissolved oxygen in marine waters.
What does upwelling bring toward the surface?
Upwelling can deliver nutrients that support productive ecosystems.
A place where river freshwater mixes with seawater
Estuaries are transition zones between rivers and the sea.
Why are mangroves valuable coastal habitats?
They provide nursery habitat and help protect shorelines
Mangroves support wildlife, trap sediment, and reduce wave energy.
A flowering plant that lives underwater
Seagrasses are marine flowering plants that create productive habitats.
Why is plastic pollution harmful in oceans?
Animals can ingest or become entangled in it
Plastic can persist, fragment, and harm marine organisms.
